{"self_assessment": "**Impact:** I picked the fish with a forked tail because its outline reads clearly on its own, and I split the work into top line, bottom line and tail. By our last trace, the start connected all 161 standing dominoes, and the outline looked like a fish to me. I didn't see the result of the push, so I can't say how the judge read it. I also never got the eye in, and I used only about 160 of the 250 dominoes, so there was room for more detail. The small stub near the nose is harmless but not clean.

**Execution:** My opening was sloppy. I said I'd put the sketch on the pad, but it was blank, and Priya had to redraw it from my description. That cost about a minute. Later I laid a fin branch and a curved joint at the belly near the start, and Maya was re-laying the same area. That was duplicated effort and a clash I should have avoided. In the second half I did better. I ran the bottom line across to the tail junction, walked the chain by eye and caught that the lower fork wasn't joined to the junction. I flagged that to Tom to fix. I also pushed for small repairs only and no new pieces once the chain was connected.

**Collaboration:** I handed out clear roles and gave Priya, Maya and Tom ownership of their pieces. I thanked people when they caught things, such as Maya's curl cleanup and Priya's nose bridge. The overlap with Maya at the belly is on me. I should have said who owned that area before I started building there.

**Leadership:** I set the plan early, kept the table focused on connectivity, and called for hands off near the end so nothing got bumped. Priya also took initiative, redrawing the pad and keeping the status updates going, so the leadership was shared. My weaknesses were the blank pad at the start and the overlap on the belly. I'd fix both next time by checking the pad myself before announcing it and by naming an owner for each area up front."}
